body: Friday, March 07 2025 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto
Information available before 2025-03-07 00:00 UTC. Prices use completed prior sessions. Prepared retrospectively; later outcomes are excluded.

Macro Stance: Tariffs have turned the US tape into a growth scare. The S&P 500 closed at 5,738.52 on 2025-03-06, down 5.33% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06), and the index group slid to four-month lows in the same session [1]. The Nasdaq 100 is off 7.41% over 20 sessions and the Russell 2000 has lost 10.78%, the sharpest drawdown of the broad US gauges, which says the market is pricing a slowdown rather than a rotation. Volatility is the clearest read: the VIX closed at 24.87, up 57.70% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). Investors have stopped treating tariff news as noise. Reuters asked whether the 'Trump put' still holds [2], and Trump himself blamed globalists for the sell-off [3]. The administration delayed some Mexico and Canada tariffs for a month [4], yet Axios reported that stocks sank anyway [5]. A reprieve that does not lift equities tells you the market is discounting the growth hit, not the policy news. WSJ reports the recession trade is back on Wall Street [6].

Rates & Curve: The 2Y closed at 3.96% and the 10Y at 4.29% at the prior close (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-06). The 10Y-2Y spread is +33 bps and the 10Y-3M spread is -5 bps, so the front end still prices cuts. Over 20 observations the 2Y is down 21 bps and the 10Y down 14 bps, which widens the spread by 7 bps: the curve is positively sloped and the 20-observation move is bull steepening (both down, 2Y down more). Over five observations the 10Y is unchanged at 0 bps, so the rally has stalled rather than reversed. The Fed is keeping the cut door open. Bloomberg reported the Fed's Waller still sees potential for two to three cuts in 2025 [7], while MarketWatch reported he eyes cuts this year but not this month [8]. Reuters flagged that parts of the Treasury market already show concern about a pause [9]. The 30Y-10Y spread is +29 bps and the long end is holding up better than the front. (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-06)

New / Most Important: The most important fact for US risk is the tariff clock. Reuters reported Trump said Mexican goods covered by USMCA will not owe tariffs until April 2 [10], which turns the trade fight into a rolling deadline rather than a single event. Carmakers were spared for a month [11]. The surveys have not rolled over yet: the ISM manufacturing index is at 50.3 points [12] and services at 53.5 points [13]. Employment is where the softening shows. ADP data showed hiring slowed in February [14] and private payrolls rose by 77,000, the smallest gain since July [15]. Layoffs are the second leg: February job cuts are the highest since the Covid peak [16], and announcements have soared to the highest since 2020 as DOGE cuts federal staff [17]. House Republicans are aiming for a vote on Tuesday to avert a shutdown [18], so the political calendar is crowded too.

Playbook ✓: Own duration and defensive equities, keep index hedges on rather than adding single-name shorts, and avoid the tariff-exposed importers until margin guidance settles. The call turns if the Nasdaq 100 closes back above its 20-session reference of 21,658.16 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-05), and it turns harder if the index closes below the 20,052.63 close of 2025-03-06. A break there would mean the growth scare is moving from prices into earnings, and that is the moment to cut beta and add protection.

Macro Stance: The euro area is in the middle of a fiscal pivot and an easing cycle at the same time. The ECB cut its key rate to 2.5% [19] and said policy is becoming meaningfully less restrictive [20]. Berlin is the reason the market is paying up for European cyclicals. Parties agreed a historic debt-brake overhaul [21], which the Guardian reported as a move to lift the brake for defence and raise defence spending [22], and Fortune reported a $1.3 trillion package [23]. The bond market is where the pivot shows first. Fortune reported a bond selloff that began in Germany is pushing borrowing costs up around the world [24], and CNBC described global bonds selling off as investors reacted to tariffs and a German paradigm shift [25].

Activity & Inflation: Inflation is easing toward target without a recession. Euro-area inflation dipped to 2.4% in February as ECB bets pointed to a sixth rate cut [26], and unemployment in the currency bloc stood at 6.2% [27]. The euro is the transmission channel: EUR/USD closed at 1.0795 dollars per euro, up 3.79% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06), and Reuters reported the euro hit a four-month peak as the dollar languished on tariff fears [28].

New / Most Important: The ECB cut and Germany's package point the same way: looser money in the core and public money into defence and infrastructure. Investors have noticed. The STOXX 600 is up 2.03% over 20 sessions, the Euro Stoxx 50 is up 3.06%, and the DAX has gained 6.93% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). The cyclical and autos names are doing the heavy lifting. BMW is up 12.06% over 20 sessions and Volkswagen preferred shares 14.39% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06), after Reuters reported European auto stocks jumped on the Trump tariff pause as Stellantis pledged more American cars [29]. The Economist's line on the defence sector, that German defence stocks have gone ballistic and armsmakers are tooling up [30], is the clearest sign the rearmament trade has moved from the policy pages into the factories.

Playbook ✓: Own European cyclicals with German fiscal exposure and the defence supply chain, and use the German bond selloff [25] as the funding check. Trim the euro-sensitive exporters if the euro keeps rallying, since the ECB's easing bias is what caps it. The call breaks if the German bond selloff spreads into bank funding costs, or if the package stalls. Reuters reported Merz is still racing to win support for the financial package [31], and that is the political risk to the whole trade. Keep the Germany-linked exposure in baskets rather than single names until the vote is in hand.

Macro Stance: Beijing has set a policy floor and is now signalling it has room to spend more. The 2025 growth goal is around 5% [32], and the deficit target is around 4% of GDP, a record [33]. Bloomberg reported the official budget deficit is the highest in more than 30 years [34]. The finance minister says China has more room to act on fiscal policy amid global uncertainty [35], and officials say more stimulus is possible if growth slows [36]. Economists are blunter: the growth goal needs much stronger stimulus if the trade war intensifies [37]. Reuters' commentary calls the stimulus so far no big bang for commodities [38], which is the honest reading of a package that is still modest against the tariff hit.

PMIs & Activity: The official non-manufacturing PMI read 50.4 in February [39], so services held up while factories absorbed the shock. The most recent manufacturing read is the January Caixin gauge, which showed factory growth slowing [40]. The trade shock is now in the policy response. Beijing retaliated with extra tariffs of up to 15% on US farm goods [41] and added 15 US companies to its export-control list [42]. Reuters reported China is targeting US soybeans and lumber in its response [43], which means the export side is where the hit will show first, and the factory PMI is the place to look for it.

Credit Impulse: Credit is the channel the market is still waiting on. The policy agenda puts the state banks first: S&P Global flagged their capital as the focus of the economic policy meeting [44]. The fiscal window is the more immediate lever. The SCMP reported Beijing has widened the fiscal window to step up spending and counter the US tariffs [45]. The government is financing the response directly rather than waiting for loan growth to do it.

Property: Property is still the drag. Longfor's bonds sank deeper into junk territory [46], which tells you developers are still paying for the last cycle. Bloomberg News reported Beijing is weighing an end to the price cap on local governments buying apartments [47], a sign the authorities want to restart demand rather than rescue developers. The policy is working in the wrong direction for the sector: a cap removal helps land sales and local budgets, but it does not solve the balance-sheet problem of the developers.

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: The policy agenda has three pieces: the deficit above, a push for technology and industry through a national venture capital guidance fund [48], and a defence budget increase of 7.2% [49]. On trade, Beijing is answering in kind. It is hitting US farm goods with duties of up to 15% [41] and banned imports of Illumina's gene sequencers right after the US tariff action [50]. Officials say China will fight to the end in the trade war, or any other war [51]. The rhetoric is a signal to domestic investors that the state will not blink, and that matters for the stimulus trade.

Markets & Flows: Hong Kong is where the stimulus trade is priced. The Hang Seng closed at 24,369.71, up 16.65% over 20 sessions and 2.75% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). The China internet ETF, KWEB, is up 18.11% over 20 sessions and 6.31% over five. The onshore Shanghai Composite is up only 3.38% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). The yuan is firm: USD/CNY is 7.2506, down 0.27% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). Goldman Sachs raised its emerging-markets target on the AI-driven China rally [52], and Yahoo framed the rally as the Mag 7 versus the Terrific 10, with China's tech stocks outperforming [53]. The ASHR CSI 300 ETF is up 5.30% over 20 sessions, a far smaller move than the offshore names.

New / Most Important: The main China story on the day is a stimulus pivot combined with a trade war Beijing says it will not lose. The market has priced the first and is still arguing about the second. Alibaba's AI reasoning model drove the stock higher [54], and its Hong Kong line rose 8.39% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). That is the kind of product news that drives a Hong Kong rally, and it is why the stimulus trade is leaning on technology rather than on the property or credit channels.

Playbook ✓: Own the Hong Kong internet and China tech as a stimulus beta, keep it small, and fund it against the trade-exposed exporters. Watch the Hang Seng: the 20-session reference close is 20,891.62 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-06), and a close back below it would say the rally is unwinding. The call turns more constructive if the onshore market starts to confirm the offshore move, and more cautious if Beijing's stimulus stays at the level of commentary. ⚠ Divergence: the onshore Shanghai Composite is up only 3.38% over 20 sessions against Hong Kong's 16.65%, and the onshore market is the one that carries domestic demand.

Macro Stance: The Bank of Japan is moving toward another hike, and the bond market got there first. The 10-year yield hit its highest level in over 15 years [55], and Japanese 10-year yields surged to near 16-year highs on rate-hike expectations and the global selloff [56]. Reuters reported that inflation risks may stir a BOJ discussion of a rate hike in May [57]. The government is signalling the same direction: the economy minister says Japan is ready to declare an end to deflation [58], and the largest union group is asking for the biggest wage-hike demand in over 30 years [59].

Activity & Currency: USD/JPY closed at 148.8980 yen per dollar, down 2.43% over 20 sessions and 0.60% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). Nikkei describes the yen at a five-month high against the dollar as traders bet on the BOJ [60], and Reuters reported traders placed a record bet on a stronger yen with further hikes in view [61]. The Nikkei 225 closed at 37,704.93, up 0.77% in the prior session and down 2.82% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). The corporate side is cooling. Capital spending fell for the first time in four years amid tariff fears [62], and Sony and Suntory are building US stockpiles as Japan faces a Trump tariff threat [63]. Yen-selling pressure has not disappeared despite the warning shot from Washington [64], so the currency is still two-way.

Playbook ✓: Keep yen exposure small and hedged, and prefer domestic names that benefit from a wage round rather than exporters that depend on a weak currency. The call changes if USD/JPY reclaims its 20-session reference of 152.6060 yen per dollar (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-06). A reclaim would mean the hike bet is fading and the exporters get their currency back; a close below 148.8980 would mean the yen is rallying on hike bets, and that is when the domestic names should be the core holding.

Macro Stance: Australia's economy is growing again on paper, but the household sector is not keeping pace. GDP rose 1.3% in the fourth quarter [65], and the economy has exited a 21-month per-capita recession [66]. Bloomberg reported the growth acceleration backs the RBA's hawkish tone [67]. The RBA's latest cut is the awkward part. AFR has a piece on the chart the RBA used to justify its latest cut [68], and the Guardian asked why the Reserve Bank waited until February to act [69]. Households are asking a different question: what has happened to savings rates after the cut [70]?

Demand & Financing: AUD/USD is at 0.6338 US dollars, up 1.09% in the prior session and 0.84% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). The ASX 200 closed at 8,094.70, down 5.00% over 20 sessions, and the banks are leading the fall: CBA is down 5.56% over 20 sessions from its 2025-02-06 reference of 162.64 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). AFR reported short sellers are ditching CBA as the sell-off doubts mount [71], and Bloomberg has CBA tipped for the worst return potential among global bank stocks [72]. The demand side is weak too. The Country Road owner says Australia is stuck in a retail recession [73], and AFR's piece says Australians are no better off than a decade ago [74]. A battered dollar helps the exporters but, as AFR puts it, is a double-edged sword for ASX stocks [75].

Playbook ✓: Stay underweight the banks and the discretionary retailers until the next RBA move is priced. Miners are the exception: Rio Tinto has signed off on a $2.8b Pilbara iron-ore project [76], but iron ore is a China call, so size it with the China divergence in mind. The call turns if CBA reclaims its 20-session reference close of 162.64 from 2025-02-06, which would mean the sell-off has run its course. The ASX 200 has already closed below its 20-session reference of 8,520.70 from 2025-02-06 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06), so the next test is a further close below 8,094.70, which would confirm the lag is becoming a recession in demand and is the moment to cut the bank exposure further.

Macro Stance: Poland's macro picture is improving from a low base. Notes From Poland reports manufacturing shows signs of recovery for the first time in almost three years [77], and Polish-language coverage framed the same PMI as the end of an almost three-year recession: 'koniec prawie trzyletniej recesji' [78]. Eurostat put Polish unemployment at a record low, joint-lowest in the EU [79]. Pay is rising: Bankier reports GUS data show Poles earned more in 2024 [80], and Pekao expects household consumption to stay strong through 2025 [81]. Inflation has not gone away. Business Insider Polska argues inflation will still rise and gives the rate-setters a strong argument for holding [82]. The politics of rates is loud: a politician appealed to the NBP to cut, arguing Poland has the most expensive loans in the EU [83].

Markets: The zloty is the strongest part of the story. USD/PLN closed at 3.8460 zloty per dollar, down 1.80% in the prior session and 4.74% over 20 sessions, and EUR/PLN is at 4.1512 zloty per euro, down 1.14% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). Bloomberg reported the zloty surged to a 10-year high, fanned by a hawkish central bank [84], and Bankier reported the euro had returned to 4.20 zloty [85]. The index is following the currency. The WIG20 total-return tracker closed at 50.12 PLN, up 7.21% over 20 sessions, and the Poland ETF EPOL is up 13.96% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). The leaders are Orlen, up 15.34%, mBank, up 14.94%, and Asseco Poland, up 15.42% over 20 sessions, with PKO Bank up 8.73%. JSW is the laggard, down 5.81% in the prior session. Foreign central banks are buying Polish treasuries [86], and more than ten of them hold the bonds [87], which is the funding backdrop for the rally.

Fiscal & Politics: Brussels is easing the excessive-deficit rules, and the Polish question is whether that helps [88]: 'Bruksela łagodzi reguły nadmiernego deficytu. Polska zyska czy straci?' The government's political calendar has a confidence vote in it. PM Tusk has put it on 11 June [89]. Budget room is tight on the cost side: Rzeczpospolita asks why power in Poland is so expensive, with CO2 costs hitting hard [90]. Banks are the political target. Money.pl reports a fight over lending margins, with the Marshal stepping in and the banks furious [91], and Business Insider Polska says big profits have become inconvenient and the banks are again the punching bag [92]. Credit holidays are not coming back, and the government is pointing to another fix [93].

Corporate & Sectors: Defence is the Polish sector story. Business Insider Polska says the armaments sector is driving share prices and names the biggest winners [94], while Bankier calls armaments the hottest commodity on the market, with shares setting fresh records [95]. Money.pl reports the government is announcing an arms build-up, but the steel industry talks of the end of an era [96]. Orlen is the energy name. It set a record for gas output, which Business Insider Polska says covers half of Poland's demand [97], and it signed a carbon-capture deal with Equinor [98]. Russian oil is no longer flowing to the Czech Republic, so Rzeczpospolita asks where Orlen will source its crude [99]. Dino keeps setting records: Business Insider Polska reports a new all-time high in a weak market [100]. The Parkiet strategist says the strong zloty is supporting the WIG20 and asks whether a new record is coming [101].

Geopolitics & Security: Security spending links the defence trade to the zloty. Poland and South Korea signed a security agreement [102], Poland's government published its security strategy under the heading of a stronger Europe and transatlantic unity [103], and Defense News reports Airbus and Boeing are both angling for a Polish tanker-aircraft deal [104]. The Russia risk is still live. Lech Wałęsa said Trump's treatment of Zelenskyy filled him with horror [105], and a Canadian teenager recruited to spy for Russia is now in a Polish jail [106].

New / Most Important: The one signal that matters is the zloty against the euro and dollar. A strong zloty lowers the cost of imports and of the defence orders, and it is lifting the index. Parkiet's strategist frames the WIG20 as riding on the currency [101], and the fear gauge is the check on that [107]: Parkiet asks what stock markets fear most, and its answer is the index of fear.

Playbook ✓: Own the WIG20 names with domestic cash flows and the defence supply chain, keep the zloty exposure on, and buy the banks only on a dip. The call changes if USD/PLN reclaims its 20-session reference of 4.0374 zloty per dollar (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-06). A reclaim would mean the currency has turned and the index loses its tailwind. ⚠ Divergence: PKO Bank and Pekao are up 8.73% and 7.79% over 20 sessions while the margin fight is the live political risk for the same banks [91], so the banks are rising on a story the politicians are already attacking.

Narrative: Semiconductors set the tone for technology. Nvidia fell 6% into a correction as the Nasdaq bled [108], and the SOX index is down 11.86% over 20 sessions and 4.53% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). The sector ETF, XLK, is down 8.01% over 20 sessions. The AI-spending doubt that sits under the drawdown is the driver that matters now, because it hits the names with the most capex-linked revenue first.

Reported: Marvell plunged nearly 20% as its outlook fell short of high expectations [109], and Reuters called it the stock's worst day in 24 years [110]. Marvell is down 19.81% in the prior session and 37.94% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). The quarter itself produced record revenue [111], which is the point: the top line was strong, and the outlook fell short of expectations.

EPS Upside Watch: The upside set-up is the names whose guide is less conservative than the market fears. Marvell's record revenue quarter [111] shows the business can grow while the outlook disappoints, so a next guide that merely matches the street would be a surprise. Watch the AI-exposed names that have not yet reported, because a stable capex signal would undo the Marvell lesson.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Loop Capital upgraded Marvell after the slide and called the post-earnings sell-off a buying opportunity [112]. That cuts against the consensus that the guide has broken the semiconductor story, and it is the signal to watch if the group rebounds while the Nasdaq stays under pressure.

Narrative: Platforms are the drag and the hope. Meta is down 10.92% over 20 sessions and 4.35% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06), and Alphabet is down 9.92% over 20 sessions. The bull case is the cloud share story, with commentary arguing Google Cloud is taking share from AWS and Azure [113].

Reported: There is no clean quarterly print for this group in the last two weeks. The company news is product and commentary: Meta is accelerating its voice-powered AI push [114], and Alphabet's CFO offered a bullish view of Waymo as the future of transportation [115]. Those are the lines the market is weighing against the sell-off.

EPS Upside Watch: Cloud share gains and AI monetisation are the upside cases. The cloud argument [113] and the Waymo framing [115] give the bulls a reason to expect the next quarter to beat, while the drawdown leaves little room for a miss to be forgiven.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Ratings are moving into the weakness. A Seeking Alpha note upgrades Alphabet on the Waymo and Willow angle [116], which runs against a sector that has been sold for platform risk rather than for its earnings.

Narrative: Credit and rates are the drivers. Financials are down 4.45% over 20 sessions and 1.65% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06), and regional banks in KRE are down 10.80% over 20 sessions. Bloomberg reported credit spreads are on the longest widening streak since 2023 [117], which is the financing side of the growth scare.

Reported: Full-year 2024 results were split. Customers Bancorp's EPS missed [118], while Merchants Bancorp beat expectations [119]. Blackstone also beat on its full-year numbers [120], which kept fee-based capital markets in the positive column.

EPS Upside Watch: Bank earnings are the wrong place to look for a surprise until the curve stops steepening on growth fears. The better set-up is the fee side, where Blackstone's beat [120] shows deal and fund revenue still clearing the bar, and where a steeper curve helps lending spreads without a credit event.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Private credit is easing off mega loan deals as banks regain ground [121], which means the lenders outside the banking system are losing share just as spreads widen. That is the convention-breaking detail: the stress is pushing business back toward the banks, not away from them.

Narrative: Oil is the sector's problem. WTI is at 66.36 dollars a barrel, down 5.67% over five sessions and 6.57% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06), and the energy ETF XLE is down 4.73% over 20 sessions. The swing factor is Iran. Reuters reported the US is weighing a plan to disrupt Iran's oil by halting vessels at sea [122], which would add a supply premium that the price has not yet carried.

Reported: BP's chief executive faces a 30% pay cut after a profit miss and an Elliott intervention [123], and Harbour Energy's shares sank to a record low after a profit hit from the UK windfall tax [124]. Aramco expects a lower 2025 dividend after net income fell [125].

EPS Upside Watch: The upside case needs price rather than volume. OPEC's February output rose as Iran's exports kept flowing [126], so the supply side is not tight. A surprise would come from the Iran premium being rebuilt, which is what the Treasury's pressure campaign would do [127].

⚡ Breaking Convention: The Treasury secretary says the US will collapse Iran's economy by shutting down its oil industry [127], which is a supply threat rather than a demand story. A deal would take the premium out fast, so any Iran news is the trigger for the sector, and the sector's own earnings are not the swing factor.

Narrative: Industrials are a tariff-exposure trade with defence and aerospace offsets. XLI is down 3.22% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06), and Boeing is down 12.87% over the same span. The supply chain is the bottleneck. Boeing is seeking a plan B after a fire destroyed a key supplier's plant [128], which is the kind of disruption that moves the whole sector's delivery schedule.

Reported: Air France-KLM's surprise profit beat lifted its shares to a five-year high [129], and CMA CGM will invest $20B in US shipping and supply-chain capabilities [130]. Those are the two reported stories that show the sector's cyclical side is not dead.

EPS Upside Watch: The defence names are the setup. Citi says Lockheed and five other defence stocks look like buys after a slump [131], and European budgets are signalling the orders that could follow, with European defence stocks already jumping on the spending pledge [132]. The upside is order flow, not a guide.

⚡ Breaking Convention: A return of the full tariffs on Canadian and Mexican goods would break any rebound in the importers, and the pause is the only thing holding that line today [5]. The sector is pricing a pause, not a settlement, which is the convention the consensus has not yet accepted.

Narrative: Consumer discretionary is the tariff casualty. XLY is down 10.09% over 20 sessions and 2.54% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06), with Tesla's 30.34% slide over 20 sessions the largest single drag on the group. Best Buy's chief warned price increases are highly likely because of tariffs [133], which is the consumer-price story the group has to absorb.

Reported: Macy's forecast 2025 sales and profit below estimates on inflation and tariff uncertainty [134], and Abercrombie & Fitch shares dropped after a tepid forecast [135]. Foot Locker's results show the sneaker industry, and Nike, still have more pain ahead [136].

EPS Upside Watch: Zalando expects higher profit and sales as it moves upmarket [137], which makes it the one reported name in the group with a guide that rises. That is the exception that proves the rule: the upside in this sector is in the companies that can keep prices up.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Retailers are asking suppliers to absorb the tariff hit. Walmart is asking Chinese suppliers for major price cuts on tariffs [138], which means the price shock is being pushed upstream rather than passed to the shopper yet. That is a break in the consumer-price narrative and a reason the margin story could hold.

Narrative: Staples are the defensive bid. XLP is up 4.40% over 20 sessions, and Coca-Cola is up 11.63% over the same span (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06), while Walmart is down 7.63%. The rotation favours the names with pricing power and the sector's ETF is still the one that holds up in a tariff scare.

Reported: Costco missed quarterly profit estimates on rising merchandise costs [139], though same-store sales beat expectations [140]. The beat and the miss sit in the same report, which is why the group is trading on comparable sales rather than headline profit.

EPS Upside Watch: Dollar General's Q4 is expected to decline [141], a preview that sets a low bar. The upside case is a guide that holds up better than the quarter, which would be the tell that the staples bid has a fundamental base rather than a rotation behind it.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Reports disagree on Reckitt. One says its shares rose after a profit beat [142], and another says they fell as the Dettol owner predicted modest growth on restructuring [143]. The convention is that staples always rise when growth scares, and this is a reminder that the sector can split on the company level.

Narrative: Healthcare is the defensive bid with a weight-loss story inside it. XLV is up 0.55% over 20 sessions, and Eli Lilly is up 8.38% over the same span (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). A federal judge stopped compounded copies of Lilly's weight-loss and diabetes drugs [144], which is the pricing protection the bulls are paying for.

Reported: Biotech roundups show Moderna up on updates [145], and two telehealth firms are turning to branded Zepbound as restrictions loom on copies [146]. Moderna is up 10.32% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06), which fits the update-driven bid.

EPS Upside Watch: The upside set-up is the branded supply chain. Telehealth firms moving to branded product [146] keep the price premium intact, and Teladoc's partnership with Lilly's direct channel [147] shows the manufacturer is widening access rather than defending a single channel.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Novo Nordisk's chief executive says he does not worry much about tariffs [148], which runs against the view that the pharma tariff risk is the sector's main threat. Novo's Copenhagen line is down 3.56% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06), so the market is not taking the CEO's word for it.

Narrative: Materials are mixed. The copper miners' ETF, COPX, is up 1.26% over 20 sessions, and the front-month copper contract is up 7.77% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06), while the materials ETF is down 1.67%. Copper is treated here as an asset, a bet on AI data-centre and grid capex, not as a gauge of growth.

Reported: MMG halted a new Congo plant after one year on a cobalt slump [149], and Rio Tinto created a lithium unit after completing its $6.7B Arcadium deal [150]. Those are capital decisions, and they tell you the bulk and battery miners are still spending into a weaker market.

A name that falls 11.17 percent on good news can gap again on the next capacity headline, so size it for that, not for the announcement.

Where It Breaks: The trigger is the SLV reference of 29.35 dollars from 5 February. SLV closed at 29.69 dollars, so a close below 29.35 would end the squeeze story for now. Dip-buyers in silver typically arrive after the first leg, which is the sign to stop chasing.

Why Retail Is Here: Meme coins were pitched as a cheap lottery ticket, and the best ones came with a celebrity name attached. Yahoo Finance reported on 4 March that Ronaldinho's STAR10 meme coin reached a $397 million market cap before dropping [221]. Yahoo Finance UK's 6 March headline says Trump's meme coin is down 81% and Melania's 92% since launch [222], and TradingView's 5 March headline says the memecoin market has crashed 56% since its December peak amid fading hype [223]. Where It Breaks: The levels are concrete. Its 20-session reference is 0.27 dollars from 14 February, so the trigger is attention returning: a recovery toward that level would show the hype coming back, while a further slide would confirm the fade. The instrument risk is the one that matters for a token. It has no earnings to fall back on, so attention is the whole price, and the first sign that attention is leaving usually shows up in the price before it shows up in a headline.

parts: Macro Stance

Tariffs have turned the US tape into a growth scare. The S&P 500 closed at 5,738.52 on 2025-03-06, down 5.33% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06), and the index group slid to four-month lows in the same session [[n11068]]. The Nasdaq 100 is off 7.41% over 20 sessions and the Russell 2000 has lost 10.78%, the sharpest drawdown of the broad US gauges, which says the market is pricing a slowdown rather than a rotation. Volatility is the clearest read: the VIX closed at 24.87, up 57.70% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). Investors have stopped treating tariff news as noise. Reuters asked whether the 'Trump put' still holds [[n11045]], and Trump himself blamed globalists for the sell-off [[n11079]]. The administration delayed some Mexico and Canada tariffs for a month [[n4835]], yet Axios reported that stocks sank anyway [[n4838]]. A reprieve that does not lift equities tells you the market is discounting the growth hit, not the policy news. WSJ reports the recession trade is back on Wall Street [[n11074]].
Rates & Curve

The 2Y closed at 3.96% and the 10Y at 4.29% at the prior close (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-06). The 10Y-2Y spread is +33 bps and the 10Y-3M spread is -5 bps, so the front end still prices cuts. Over 20 observations the 2Y is down 21 bps and the 10Y down 14 bps, which widens the spread by 7 bps: the curve is positively sloped and the 20-observation move is bull steepening (both down, 2Y down more). Over five observations the 10Y is unchanged at 0 bps, so the rally has stalled rather than reversed. The Fed is keeping the cut door open. Bloomberg reported the Fed's Waller still sees potential for two to three cuts in 2025 [[n11039]], while MarketWatch reported he eyes cuts this year but not this month [[n11040]]. Reuters flagged that parts of the Treasury market already show concern about a pause [[n10889]]. The 30Y-10Y spread is +29 bps and the long end is holding up better than the front. (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-06)

The most important fact for US risk is the tariff clock. Own European cyclicals with German fiscal exposure and the defence supply chain, and use the German bond selloff [[n3553]] as the funding check. Keep the Germany-linked exposure in baskets rather than single names until the vote is in hand.

Beijing has set a policy floor and is now signalling it has room to spend more. The 2025 growth goal is around 5% [[n1357]], and the deficit target is around 4% of GDP, a record [[n1359]]. Reuters' commentary calls the stimulus so far no big bang for commodities [[n1478]], which is the honest reading of a package that is still modest against the tariff hit.
PMIs & Activity

The official non-manufacturing PMI read 50.4 in February [[n0985]], so services held up while factories absorbed the shock. The most recent manufacturing read is the January Caixin gauge, which showed factory growth slowing [[n0487]]. The trade shock is now in the policy response. Beijing retaliated with extra tariffs of up to 15% on US farm goods [[n1187]] and added 15 US companies to its export-control list [[n1173]]. Reuters reported China is targeting US soybeans and lumber in its response [[n1190]], which means the export side is where the hit will show first, and the factory PMI is the place to look for it.
Credit Impulse

Credit is the channel the market is still waiting on. The policy agenda puts the state banks first: S&P Global flagged their capital as the focus of the economic policy meeting [[n1193]]. The fiscal window is the more immediate lever. The SCMP reported Beijing has widened the fiscal window to step up spending and counter the US tariffs [[n1369]]. The government is financing the response directly rather than waiting for loan growth to do it.
Property

Property is still the drag. Longfor's bonds sank deeper into junk territory [[n1387]], which tells you developers are still paying for the last cycle. Bloomberg News reported Beijing is weighing an end to the price cap on local governments buying apartments [[n1490]], a sign the authorities want to restart demand rather than rescue developers. The policy is working in the wrong direction for the sector: a cap removal helps land sales and local budgets, but it does not solve the balance-sheet problem of the developers.
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

The policy agenda has three pieces: the deficit above, a push for technology and industry through a national venture capital guidance fund [[n1492]], and a defence budget increase of 7.2% [[n1191]]. On trade, Beijing is answering in kind. It is hitting US farm goods with duties of up to 15% [[n1187]] and banned imports of Illumina's gene sequencers right after the US tariff action [[n1177]]. Officials say China will fight to the end in the trade war, or any other war [[n1493]]. The rhetoric is a signal to domestic investors that the state will not blink, and that matters for the stimulus trade.

Tariffs could raise prices for new homes [[n1437]], which would undo the mortgage relief if builders pass the cost on. The convention is that falling rates lift home-related REITs, and the tariff cost on building materials is the break in that chain.
Narrative

Utilities are the hangover from the AI-power trade. XLU is down 3.20% over 20 sessions, and the AI-power names have fallen much further: Constellation Energy is down 33.82% and Vistra down 33.33% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). The group has been bought for data-centre demand and sold when the deal flow slowed.
Reported

NuScale's US small-modular-reactor deals remain elusive, Utility Dive reported [[n3027]], and Oklo closed its acquisition of the radioisotope producer Atomic Alchemy [[n6334]]. The reactor names are down far more than the regulated utilities: Oklo is down 48.57% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06).
EPS Upside Watch

Power demand is the upside case. Yahoo has argued the bull case for Vistra again [[n9261]], and the drawdown has left the earnings base cheaper than the story. The upside arrives if the data-centre contracts that the market has been waiting for start to land.
⚡ Breaking Convention

CNBC reports the power stock at the centre of the AI trade is fading while impatient investors await a data-centre deal [[n6048]]. The convention is that power names are a hedge on AI capex. The break is that they are falling with it, so the deal flow is the only thing that changes the trade.
Narrative

European autos are the tariff-relief trade. The iShares STOXX Europe 600 Automobiles ETF, the SXAP tracker, is up 1.68% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06), and BMW is up 12.06% over the same span. Reuters reported European auto stocks jumped on the Trump tariff pause as Stellantis pledged more American cars [[n3544]].
Reported

Tesla's German car sales kept falling in February [[n10522]], which is the weak spot in the group. Stellantis pledged more American-built cars [[n3544]], a move that shows the makers are re-routing supply rather than absorbing the tariff cost.
EPS Upside Watch

Volkswagen may avoid a 25% Trump tariff while BMW and others face a trade levy [[n9258]], so the upside depends on which maker gets the carve-out. The set-up is a company-by-company tariff outcome, which is why the sector ETF can rise while individual names split.
⚡ Breaking Convention

European autos sank as US tariffs on Mexico and Canada kicked in [[n3406]], and then rallied on the pause [[n3544]]. The same sector moved in opposite directions within days, which means the pause is the trade rather than a settled tariff outcome.
Narrative

US–Asia semis are the most crowded part of the technology trade and the largest drawdown among the sector ETFs. SOXX is down 10.22% over 20 sessions and 4.16% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). The SOX index is down 11.86% over the same period. The driver is the AI spending doubt that sits under the Nvidia and Marvell sell-offs.
Reported

TSMC's chief executive says the US investment is driven by customer demand [[n8976]], and TSMC's Arizona fab production is sold out through late 2027 [[n9184]]. Those are the strongest order signals in the last two weeks, and the stock has not yet priced them.
EPS Upside Watch

OpenAI and Oracle are eyeing Nvidia chips worth billions for the Stargate site [[n9136]]. That is the demand the drawdown is treating as temporary. If the next capex guide confirms it, the group's earnings base is better than the price suggests.
⚡ Breaking Convention

ASML is building a reuse-and-repair centre in Beijing despite US–China tech tensions [[n3044]], which cuts against the sell-off story that export controls shut China out of the chain. A company that keeps investing in China is a signal that the controls are not the whole story.

earnings_pattern.title: Guidance, not the quarter, sets the reaction
parts: Rewarded

Air France-KLM's surprise profit beat lifted its shares to a five-year high [[n2932]], the clearest case of a beat being rewarded. Adidas's fourth-quarter sales topped expectations even as its final Yeezy stock sold off [[n2931]]. Blackstone beat on its full-year 2024 numbers [[n2948]], and Samsara's fourth quarter beat on both earnings and revenue [[n3121]].
Punished

The punishment went to guidance. Marvell's outlook fell short of high expectations and the shares slid nearly 20% in the prior session [[n3105]], with the price down 37.94% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). MongoDB's shares sank after it issued weak guidance [[n2989]], and the stock is down 26.46% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). Best Buy's chief warned that price increases were highly likely because of tariffs [[n2837]], and Continental's shares plunged on a revenue fall and soft guidance [[n2845]].
Pattern

The pattern is that the beat is not the trade; the guide is. CrowdStrike beat its fourth-quarter estimates [[n2848]], yet the stock is down 8.55% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). Costco missed on profit [[n3069]] while its same-store sales beat [[n3146]], and the shares were soft in the prior session. Marvell's record revenue quarter [[n2983]] did not protect the stock once the outlook disappointed. A beat that does not lift the guide gets no credit from the market.
Attention into EPS

The next set of prints is being framed around the outlook. Dollar General's fourth quarter is expected to decline [[n3075]], and Constellation Software's fourth-quarter preview asks investors what to look for [[n0463]]. Post-earnings drift is already visible in the auto-screen pieces: Cummins is down 6.1% since its last report [[n0466]], and Marathon Petroleum is down 14.1% [[n0467]]. The drift is the warning that the first print was not the whole story.
Playbook

Trade the guide, not the quarter. Buy a punished name after a guide reset only when the next outlook is set low enough to beat, as Marvell's post-slide upgrade argues [[n9097]], and avoid chasing beats where the outlook is cut. Size into the outlook for the pre-report names, not the quarter. The call is invalidated if a guide that holds fails to bring the price back, because then the reaction was about positioning, and waiting is the cheaper trade.

underowned.title: China and Hong Kong internet
parts: Attention Gap

The coverage is about the AI story and institutional calls rather than about the domestic investor base. Goldman Sachs raised its emerging-markets target on the AI-driven China rally [[n1509]], and Yahoo framed the move as the Mag 7 against the Terrific 10 [[n1521]]. The attention is institutional, which is the gap: a rally of this size in the offshore names is being sold to professionals, not explained to the household.
Exposure & Risk

KWEB is up 18.11% over 20 sessions, FXI up 15.78%, and the Hang Seng up 16.65% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). The US-listed Alibaba line is up 40.96% over 20 sessions. The risk is the trade war, since Beijing says it will fight to the end [[n1493]], and the offshore names are the most exposed to a news reversal.
Trigger to Watch

A Hang Seng close back below its 20-session reference of 20,891.62 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-06) would signal the theme is losing its footing. The upside trigger is the next stimulus step, which the finance minister says China has the room to take [[n1488]].

underowned.title: European cyclicals outside defence
parts: Attention Gap

Investors are gradually regaining their appetite for Europe [[n3498]], but the coverage is still dominated by defence and by the German package. Broad European cyclicals, from banks to industrials, get less attention than the armaments names, which is why the gap is still there.
Exposure & Risk

The broad European ETF VGK is up 6.25% over 20 sessions and FEZ up 7.57% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06), with the DAX up 6.93% and the STOXX 600 up 2.03%. The risk is the bond selloff that began in Germany and spread around the world [[n3530]], which lifts the cost of capital for the same cyclicals the trade is buying.
Trigger to Watch
Merz is still racing to win the votes for the financial package [[n3482]]. A passed package is the event that moves this from an underowned theme into a consensus one; a failed vote reverses it.

underowned.title: Copper miners as an asset
parts: Attention Gap

Money.pl's piece on copper's future argues Europe must bet on mining development [[n5622]], which is the policy framing. The price has moved more than the equities: front-month copper is up 7.77% over 20 sessions and the copper miners' ETF COPX only 1.26% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). The attention is on the metal, the equity is still lagging.
Exposure & Risk

Freeport-McMoRan is up 2.73% over 20 sessions, and COPX is the instrument for the basket. The risk is supply-side disruption rather than demand: MMG halted a new Congo plant after one year on a cobalt slump [[n9087]], and that is a reminder that the supply side is still fragile.
Trigger to Watch

The copper front month closed at 4.78 dollars a pound against a 20-session reference of 4.43 dollars a pound (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-05). With the front month already above that reference and the miners lagging, a further close above 4.78 dollars a pound would confirm the metal is leading the equities, which makes the miners the cheap expression of the same asset.

underowned.title: US small caps and regional banks
parts: Attention Gap

MarketWatch's piece on investors worried about Trump and the group they are buying instead is about a 'forgotten' group of stocks [[n10875]], and it is the nearest thing to a small-cap story in the news. The coverage is thin compared with the mega-cap drawdown.
Exposure & Risk

The Russell 2000 is down 10.78% over 20 sessions, IWM down 10.51%, and the regional-bank ETF KRE down 10.80% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). The risk is credit: Bloomberg reported spreads on their longest widening streak since 2023 [[n3698]], which is the financing pressure that hits small caps first.
Trigger to Watch

A Russell 2000 close back above its 20-session reference of 2,316.23 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-05) would mean the group is recovering the ground it lost in the growth scare. Until then the theme stays underowned, and the trigger is a tariff clarity event rather than an earnings beat.

crypto.title: Reserve headlines, uneven tokens
parts: Market Context

Bitcoin closed at 89,961.73 dollars on the prior completed daily close, down 7.74% over 20 sessions from 97,508.97 dollars on 2025-02-14 but up 4.57% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-06). Ether is down 19.21% over 20 sessions from 2,726.09 dollars and Solana is down 28.30% from 199.94 dollars, while Dogecoin is down 25.82% over the same span. The majors are not moving together. XRP is up 18.77% over five sessions and 4.05% in the prior session. The equities show the same split: Coinbase is down 22.16% over 20 sessions, Strategy is up 26.69% over five, and the iShares bitcoin trust IBIT is up 6.95% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06).
New / Most Important

The reserve is the new fact. Trump signed an executive order to establish a government bitcoin reserve [[n2078]], and Fortune reports the order adds 200,000 seized bitcoins [[n2080]]. Bitcoin still fell after the reserve was officially set up [[n2019]], which means the policy was largely priced before it arrived. Barron's reports bitcoin dipping below $90,000 again [[n2014]]. The White House's first crypto summit is on Friday [[n6366]], so the policy calendar runs through the report date itself, and the market has to decide whether the summit adds substance or only ceremony.
Playbook

Hold a small bitcoin core and trade the reserve news as a sell-the-news event rather than a trend. Keep ether underweight while its 20-session drop is 19.21%, and treat XRP's five-session surge as a trade, not a holding. The trigger is bitcoin's 20-session reference of 97,508.97 dollars (2025-02-14): a close back above it would say the reserve is acting as a price floor, while a close that fails below the 89,961.73 level would say the buy-the-rumour trade has failed for now.

flows.title: Liquidity is still there, but the price of it is rising
parts: Global Liquidity

The euro area is easing: the ECB cut its key rate to 2.5% [[n3538]], and the ECB says policy is becoming meaningfully less restrictive [[n3543]]. Japan is moving the other way, with the BOJ discussion of a May hike in view [[n5247]]. China is widening its fiscal window to counter the tariffs [[n1369]]. The liquidity read closest to the US market comes from the New York Fed, which says market liquidity levels remain abundant [[n3939]]. The front end is still pricing easing: the 3M is at 4.34% against a 2Y at 3.96% (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-06). The Bank of England is more cautious and warned tariffs could hit UK consumers [[n3452]].
Rates & Dollar

The dollar is losing its bid. The Dollar Index closed at 104.06 index points, down 3.27% over 20 sessions and 1.59% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). Reuters reported the dollar is set to lose its lustre on trade-war jitters [[n3969]], and Business Insider argues a weaker dollar might not be a great sign for the US [[n3966]]. The 10Y is at 4.29% and the 2Y at 3.96%, with the 10Y down 14 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-06). HYG is at 79.32 dollars and down 0.50% over 20 sessions, TLT is at 90.40 dollars and up 0.57% over 20, and LQD is at 108.49 dollars, up 0.27% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06).
Credit Check

Credit is where the growth scare gets priced. Bloomberg reported credit spreads are on the longest widening streak since 2023 [[n3698]], and the high-yield ETF is softer than the investment-grade one: HYG is down 0.50% over 20 sessions while LQD is up 0.27%. A controversial private-credit ETF faces new regulatory hurdles [[n9316]], and WSJ reported private credit is easing off mega-loan deals as banks regain ground [[n1423]]. The spread move matters more than its level: HYG is down 0.74% over five sessions, so high yield has been weakening in the last week rather than the last month (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). The picture is a credit market that is repricing risk without yet closing its doors.
Equity & Fund Flows

Flow coverage is driven by news, and the stories point to access rather than to buying. Washington is signalling plans to open private funds to more investors [[n4014]]. Millennium is backing Janus Henderson's stockpicker Ben Wallace with $1 billion [[n3841]]. Morningstar says bonds take the lead over stocks in 2025 [[n3990]]. Mars priced an eight-part, $26 billion bond [[n3933]], a sign the financing window for large deals is open. Zero-day options trading hit a record on the Trump turmoil and the Robinhood push [[n6162]], which is the retail-flow channel that matters for the speculative names, and it is the first place a reversal shows up.
Portfolio Implication

Keep liquidity exposure in the front end and in short-duration credit, avoid high yield while spreads keep widening, and hold dollar shorts only through the cyclical beneficiaries [[n3969]]. The bond market is doing the work: the 2Y is down 21 bps over 20 observations and the curve is steepening on the easing side. The front end is the cheapest place to hold cash-like risk while the curve steepens, since the 3M at 4.34% against a 2Y at 3.96% says the market still expects cuts (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-06). The invalidation is simple. If HYG reclaims its 20-session reference of 79.72 dollars (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-05), credit is repairing and the defensive stance can come off.

anticipatory.title: A House vote on the shutdown
parts: What Is Priced

House Republicans are aiming for a vote on Tuesday to avert a shutdown [[n11083]], and Reuters' explainer sets out what a shutdown would mean for the government [[n11037]]. The market is pricing the vote as a procedural event. Democrats are not simply going along: Politico reports they are serious about a shutdown [[n10852]], and Axios says Senate Democrats are warming to helping the GOP avoid one [[n10993]].
Conditional Expression

If the House vote passes and the Senate follows, the political premium fades and the market goes back to the growth data and the tariff clock. The rates trade keeps its bull-steepening bias, and the cyclicals regain some ground. If the vote fails, the shelter trade is Treasuries and the dollar's safe-haven bid, while the cyclical and small-cap names are the first to give back their gains. Either way the Treasury curve is the instrument that tells you which path the market believes.
Risk

The risk is that a shutdown becomes a second leg of the growth scare rather than a one-off. Federal layoffs are already in the news [[n10587]], so a shutdown would compound the cuts. The VIX at 24.87 is the gauge to watch, since it has already risen 57.70% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06) and has the room to go higher on a political shock.

anticipatory.title: The tariff clock
parts: What Is Priced

The market is pricing the tariff pauses as a reprieve. Trump said Mexican goods covered by USMCA will not owe tariffs until April 2 [[n4808]], and the Mexico and Canada delay is for one month [[n4835]]. Carmakers have their own one-month exemption [[n4719]]. The equity market is not convinced: the S&P 500 fell to four-month lows even with the pause in place [[n11068]].
Conditional Expression

If the pause is extended, autos and importers recover: the European autos tracker is up 1.68% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06), and the rebound would extend to the US carmakers. If the pause lapses on schedule, the trade is a repeat of the early-March auto selloff, when European auto stocks sank as the tariffs took effect [[n3406]]. The trade is the deadline itself, so position around the date rather than through it.
Risk

The pause is the trade, and a lapse is a fresh shock to every tariff-exposed name. Canadian and Mexican carmakers are the most exposed, and the market has shown it will sell the pause news even when the pause is granted [[n4838]]. The risk is that the market learns the pause is a negotiating tool rather than a settlement.

anticipatory.title: The crypto summit and the reserve
parts: What Is Priced

The reserve is partly priced. Bitcoin fell after the reserve was officially established [[n2019]], which says the market had already marked the policy into the price. The White House's first crypto summit is on Friday [[n6366]], and the next statement may add the substance the first order lacked. The market's question is whether the summit names the assets, which would move the tokens, or stays at the level of bitcoin.
Conditional Expression

If the summit adds named assets, the reserve tokens get the squeeze that XRP has already started to show, with XRP up 18.77% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-06). If it is a policy speech with no assets, the reserve becomes a sell-the-news event and bitcoin's 20-session drop of 7.74% extends. The position should be sized to the two outcomes, not to the summit itself.
Risk

The reserve is the one policy in the story that is discretionary, so it can be expanded, narrowed or delayed without a vote. Skeptics are already on the record: bitcoin maximalists have a bone to pick with the administration [[n1806]], and crypto leaders trashed the reserve plan in the days before the order [[n1805]]. That is the dissent a summit will have to answer.

anticipatory.title: The German package vote
parts: What Is Priced

The German financing package is priced into the cyclicals. Merz is racing to win support for the package [[n3482]], and the DAX is up 6.93% over 20 sessions while BMW is up 12.06% over the same span (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). The market has treated the package as a done deal for the rearmament trade. The Bund selloff shows that the funding cost is rising [[n3530]].
Conditional Expression

If the package passes, the financing reaches the cyclicals and the defence supply chain, and the steeper German curve becomes the signal to hold. If it stalls, the German trade reverses, and the bond rally that was building before the package returns as the funding fear fades. The trade is the vote, so the entry point belongs after the vote, not before it.
Risk

The risk is the cost of the money itself. The same selloff that lifts the German trade raises borrowing costs, and CNBC reports global bonds sold off on the tariffs and a German paradigm shift [[n3553]], so a package that passes into a weak bond market can squeeze the margins of the companies it is meant to help. The bond market is the referee on this trade.

catalysts.title: $MRVL — the dip after the guide
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Marvell's outlook fell short of high expectations and the shares plunged nearly 20% in the prior session [[n3105]], a slide Reuters called the stock's worst day in 24 years [[n3106]]. Loop Capital upgraded the stock and called the post-earnings sell-off a buying opportunity [[n9097]]. The thesis is that the revenue line is intact, the record quarter [[n2983]] proves the business is growing, and the guide has been reset to a level the company can beat.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The stock closed at 72.28 dollars, down 19.81% in the prior session and 37.94% over 20 sessions from 116.46 dollars on 2025-02-05 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). The hurdle is the next report: a second guide cut would confirm the reset was not a reset. The risk is the AI capex doubt that is driving the whole semiconductor group lower.
Trade Expression

Buy a starter position on the dip and add only if the stock holds the prior session's level. Use shares rather than short-dated options, given the size of the gap risk. The trade is invalidated if the next guide is cut again or if the group's capex signal turns down.

catalysts.title: $LLY — the copies ruling
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

A federal judge stopped compounded copies of Eli Lilly's weight-loss and diabetes drugs [[n9009]], and two telehealth firms are turning to branded Zepbound as restrictions loom on copies [[n3135]]. The thesis is pricing protection: the branded product holds its premium when the copy market is cut back, and the manufacturer is widening access through its own channels [[n9191]].
Price Hurdle & Risk

The stock closed at 912.76 dollars, down 1.82% in the prior session and up 8.38% over 20 sessions from 842.18 dollars on 2025-02-05 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). The risk is that the court ruling is narrowed or reversed, and that the telehealth firms find a way around the restrictions.
Trade Expression

Own the shares as the core position, and use a call spread if you want leverage to the copy-restriction story. The trade is invalidated if branded pricing is cut to meet the copy market, since that would remove the premium the thesis depends on.

catalysts.title: $TSLA — the drawdown is the politics
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Tesla shares slid as Wall Street turned its back on Elon Musk [[n9205]], and Tesla's German car sales kept falling in February [[n10522]]. The bull case is the analyst view: Morgan Stanley sees the stock reaching $430 and reinstated it as its top pick [[n6113]]. The thesis is that the sell-off is about the politics of the chief executive rather than the car business, and the case is open until the sales data confirms otherwise.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The stock closed at 263.45 dollars, down 5.61% in the prior session, 6.56% over five sessions and 30.34% over 20 sessions from 378.17 dollars on 2025-02-05 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). The hurdle is the Morgan Stanley target of $430, well above the close [[n6113]]. The risk is the sales line, which the analysts have not yet reconciled with the price.
Trade Expression

No position until the analyst case and the sales case agree. If you want exposure, use a defined-risk call structure rather than shares. The trade is invalidated if the German sales decline continues into the next data release or if the political backlash moves from protest into lost contracts.

catalysts.title: $BA — the supplier fire
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Boeing is seeking a plan B after a fire destroyed a key supplier's plant [[n8962]], and Boeing's stock is down 12.87% over 20 sessions. The thesis is that a single-supplier loss pushes the delivery schedule out, which hits the cash conversion the stock is priced on.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The stock closed at 158.43 dollars, down 2.90% in the prior session, 8.86% over five sessions and 12.87% over 20 sessions from 181.84 dollars on 2025-02-05 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). The hurdle is the supplier's output recovery. The risk is that the plan B is quick and the market has already priced the delay.
Trade Expression
Underweight the shares or buy short-dated puts if you want the event. The trade is invalidated if the supplier restores output quickly or if Boeing's plan B is announced with a firm date.

catalysts.title: $DELL — the buyback floor
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Dell boosted its dividend by 18% and launched a $10 billion buyback [[n3701]], and its full-year EPS beat expectations [[n0433]]. The thesis is that the capital return sets a floor under the shares while the AI-server orders are reset, and the buyback gives the company a bid through the drawdown.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The stock closed at 93.02 dollars, down 4.35% in the prior session, 13.73% over five sessions and 10.94% over 20 sessions from 104.45 dollars on 2025-02-05 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). The hurdle is the buyback pace versus the price. The risk is the server-demand story, which the rest of the AI-hardware group is already marking down.
Trade Expression
Buy shares on a dip toward the recent lows, with a stop set below the current close. The trade is invalidated if the buyback is paused or if the server orders are cut in the next guide.

catalysts.title: $COIN — the tokenisation push
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Coinbase renewed its push for tokenised securities as the Trump administration emboldens the crypto industry [[n2029]], and Barron's has argued Coinbase Global could be takeover bait [[n1931]]. The thesis is an exchange that gains from every policy step, with the tokenisation product as the new revenue line.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The stock closed at 214.17 dollars, down 3.72% in the prior session, 2.78% over five sessions and 22.16% over 20 sessions from 275.14 dollars on 2025-02-05 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). The hurdle is bitcoin's direction: the stock trades with the reserve trade, and the bitcoin close is the check on the thesis.
Trade Expression

Hold a small position and hedge it with bitcoin exposure rather than adding leverage. The trade is invalidated if the reserve news fades and bitcoin fails to reclaim its 20-session reference of 97,508.97 dollars for good.

spec.retail_intro: The dominant popular-narrative trade right now is the quantum dip, a technology story with the mechanics of the 1999 infrastructure trade: the technology is real, the drawdown is long, and dip-buyers are early on the price.

retail.title: IonQ / IONQ — buy the quantum dip
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The oldest pitch in quantum is that the next computing revolution is cheap today. The Motley Fool asked on 3 March whether Rigetti or IonQ is the better quantum stock [[n6087]], and Yahoo Finance's column is headlined 'If I Could Only Buy 1 Quantum Computing Stock, This Would Be It' [[n6568]]. Dip-buyers typically look for the cheapest entry, and the 20-session reference of 42.32 dollars from 5 February is the level the stock has fallen away from. IonQ closed at 20.48 dollars (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06).
What Is Driving It

The price is the most numeric part of the story. IonQ fell 9.50 percent in the prior session, 17.78 percent over five sessions and 51.61 percent over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). The quantum group did not fall in lockstep: D-Wave lost 6.61 percent over the same session, while Rigetti rose 4.03 percent and is still down 38.47 percent over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). Nvidia dropped 5.74 percent, the Nasdaq 100 fell 2.79 percent and the VIX rose 13.41 percent to 24.87 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06), so the broad tape was weak as well. The company news kept coming anyway. IonQ acquires ID Quantique to advance global quantum networking [[n6221]] on 4 March, commissioned a quantum system at the US Air Force Research Lab [[n6219]] the same day, and reported a milestone in faster quantum gates [[n6313]] on 5 March. The catalysts did not hold the price. The 10-year yield fell 14 basis points over 20 observations to 4.29 percent (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-06), so the rate backdrop was not the drag.
The Social Signal

Attention arrives as advice, and the advice is to buy quantum. The Motley Fool asks which quantum stock is the better buy, Rigetti or IonQ [[n6087]], and Yahoo Finance's 5 March headline says a Magnificent Seven stock 'just joined the quantum computing revolution' and hints that it is not Nvidia [[n6326]]. Investor's Business Daily goes further and frames the drop as a crash triggered by Nvidia's chief executive, pointing to a Quantum Day that it ties to the same executive [[n6394]]. The usual reading is that the revolution is still under way and the drop is a price rather than a verdict. Advice columns have pushed that reading since late February, which makes the drawdown a test of conviction.
Historical Analog

The mechanical analog is the 1999 infrastructure trade, and Quartz is already drawing the comparison, asking what the dot-com burst says about stocks today [[n9222]]. The mechanism has two waves. First comes a technology that is real: the build-out is coming, and the shares price the revolution before the revenue arrives. Second comes the crowd, buying each leg down because the technology looks proven right. Retail tends to arrive in that second wave. Quantum has milestones to point to, and The Investor asks whether Microsoft's new quantum chip is a game changer [[n6111]], yet the shares have lost more than half of their value over 20 sessions. The mechanical lesson is that a technology can be right while the shares are early by years, and the buyers who were early on the price are the ones who wait longest to be paid.
Smart Money View

The institutional coverage is curious rather than certain, and the split is about the timeline, not the direction of the technology. Davy asks whether quantum computing is the next big technology [[n8012]], and The Dispatch explains Microsoft's quantum computing breakthrough [[n7929]]. Scientific American's headline says quantum confusion keeps coming with qubits [[n8679]], which is the sceptic's line. The hinge is Nvidia. Investor's Business Daily ties the crash to its chief executive [[n6394]], and Nvidia fell 5.74 percent in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). Institutions tend to read a drop like this as a timing call rather than a verdict on the technology, so the question for them is when the revenue arrives, not whether the physics works.
When the Narrative Breaks

The triggers are specific. The close is 20.48 dollars and the 20-session reference is 42.32 dollars from 5 February (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). A close below 20.48 turns the dip into a trend, and the round 20-dollar level is the next line traders tend to watch. The relative test is Rigetti: it rose 4.03 percent in the prior session while IonQ fell 9.50 percent, so if IonQ keeps falling while the rest of the quantum group holds, the dip is name-specific rather than a sector bid. The pending test is the Quantum Day that IBD ties to Nvidia's chief executive [[n6394]], and any product or customer headline from the company's own news flow would test the bull case the advice columns repeat. The instrument risk is the size of the move. A name down 51.61 percent over 20 sessions can gap several times its daily range, so size the position for a sharp reversal, not for the thesis.

retail.title: Nebius / NBIS — retail's elated over the data centre
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Stocktwits put the crowd's reaction into one headline on 5 March: Nebius rallied on plans for a 300MW data centre in New Jersey, and retail's elated [[n6365]]. Nebius sells AI capacity, so a new 300 MW site is more capacity to sell, and 300 MW is the figure the bull case leans on. Yahoo Finance's same-day report announced the site and added capacity in Kansas City and Iceland [[n6328]]. On 6 March Data Center Dynamics reported that DataOne will build the New Jersey data centre [[n6383]], which gives the bull case a reason to resume.
Where It Breaks

The levels are specific. Nebius closed at 26.80 dollars, down 11.17 percent in the prior session and 16.38 percent over five sessions, and it is 21.01 percent below its 33.93-dollar reference from 5 February (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06). The trigger is the reversal itself: a stock that drew a retail cheer on Wednesday and fell double digits the next session is the kind of reversal that says the news was priced. A close back above 33.93 dollars would mean the data-centre story has its bid back. The instrument risk is the single-stock gap. A name that falls 11.17 percent on good news can gap again on the next capacity headline, so size it for that, not for the announcement.

retail.title: Silver / SLV — the squeeze is coming
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Silver is pitched as the cheap version of gold for buyers who missed gold. Kitco asks whether a coming silver squeeze could push the metal to $250-$500, which Eric Sprott calls entirely possible [[n8977]], and Kitco's own piece argues silver's time to shine is now [[n9310]]. The Economist's line that silver is the new gold [[n6361]] is the easiest hook. The price is still moderate: SLV is up 4.54% over five sessions and 1.16% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06), and silver futures are up 3.97% over five sessions and closed at 33.06 dollars an ounce.
Where It Breaks

The trigger is the SLV reference of 29.35 dollars from 5 February. SLV closed at 29.69 dollars, so a close below 29.35 would end the squeeze story for now. The instrument risk is the difference between the ETF and the futures: the ETF tracks the metal with premiums and fees, and the futures require margin, so the trade has to be sized in one of them. The narrative breaks if the dollar rallies again, since the dollar index is down 3.27% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-06) and a reversal would hit precious metals first. Dip-buyers in silver typically arrive after the first leg, which is the sign to stop chasing.

retail.title: Dogecoin / DOGE-USD — the meme coin dream is fading
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Meme coins were pitched as a cheap lottery ticket, and the best ones came with a celebrity name attached. Yahoo Finance reported on 4 March that Ronaldinho's STAR10 meme coin reached a $397 million market cap before dropping [[n6241]]. Yahoo Finance UK's 6 March headline says Trump's meme coin is down 81% and Melania's 92% since launch [[n2082]], and TradingView's 5 March headline says the memecoin market has crashed 56% since its December peak amid fading hype [[n6325]]. The politics story is still live: Decrypt asks what the Dogecoin community makes of Elon Musk's DOGE [[n2051]].
Where It Breaks

The levels are concrete. Dogecoin closed at 0.20 dollars, down 1.46 percent in the prior session, 2.33 percent over five sessions and 25.82 percent over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-06). Its 20-session reference is 0.27 dollars from 14 February, so the trigger is attention returning: a recovery toward that level would show the hype coming back, while a further slide would confirm the fade. The instrument risk is the one that matters for a token. It has no earnings to fall back on, so attention is the whole price, and the first sign that attention is leaving usually shows up in the price before it shows up in a headline.
